test_title: SSC Selection Post 2024 (Higher Secondary Level) Official Paper (Held On: 20 Jun, 2024 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: If 8 men or 16 women or 32 boys can do a piece of work in 8 months, then in how many months can 4 men, 4 women and 4 boys together complete the work?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For 'AND/OR' type questions, use direct formula:

Time = Given Time ÷ (M₂/M₁ + W₂/W₁ + B₂/B₁)

⇒ Time = 8 ÷ (4/8 + 4/16 + 4/32)

⇒ Time = 8 ÷ (1/2 + 1/4 + 1/8) = 8 ÷ (7/8)

⇒ Time = (8 × 8) ÷ 7 = 64 ÷ 7 = 9 ¹⁄₇ months

**∴ The correct answer is 9 ¹⁄₇ months.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

8 men or 16 women or 32 boys can complete the piece of work in 8 months.

⇒ Time taken by 1 Man = 8 × 8 = 64 months

⇒ Time taken by 1 Woman = 16 × 8 = 128 months

⇒ Time taken by 1 Boy = 32 × 8 = 256 months

⇒ Total efficiency of 4 Men, 4 Women, and 4 Boys = (4 × 4) + (4 × 2) + (4 × 1)

⇒ Combined efficiency = 16 + 8 + 4 = 28 units/month

⇒ Time required = Total Work ÷ Combined efficiency

⇒ Time required = 256 ÷ 28 = 64 ÷ 7 = 9 ¹⁄₇ months

**∴ The correct answer is 9 ¹⁄₇ months.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Chain Rule (MDH Concept)

If M₁ persons can do W₁ work in D₁ days working H₁ hours/day, and M₂ persons can do W₂ work in D₂ days working H₂ hours/day, then (M₁ × D₁ × H₁) / W₁ = (M₂ × D₂ × H₂) / W₂.

Efficiency and Time

Time taken to complete a work is inversely proportional to efficiency. If the efficiency ratio of A and B is x : y, then the ratio of time taken by them to complete the work is y : x.

Work and Wages

Wages are always distributed in proportion to the total work done by an individual. If individuals work for the same number of days, the wages are distributed in the direct ratio of their efficiencies.
